items.Problem: Blood-draw reports came from many partner labs, each with its own units. An external vendor, paid about Rs. 75K a month, handled only three labs, converting their reports into Excel and mapping them with a hard-coded template and unit conversion for each lab. For every other lab, the diagnostic team typed each parameter in by hand and converted the units manually, about 20 minutes per report, with 10 to 12 reports on an average day. Unfinished reports carried over to the next day, and every new lab meant either another hard-coded template or more manual work, which did not scale as lab collaborations grew.
items.What I did: I conceptualised an AI agent that reads the blood-draw PDF, updates the investigation section and informs the team. I chose an agent over fixed rules because there are multiple vendors with multiple units: rules would have to be built for each one to match Twin's standardised units, and each data point may or may not need conversion, which an agent can decide. The agent parses the PDF and checks each parameter against Twin's standard parameters and units. Matching parameters are mapped directly. For the rest, it finds the partner's unit, converts the value to Twin's unit and checks it against the reference range. Values within range pass without a flag, and values that look unusually low or high create a task for the diagnostic team. Before relying on it, I ran the agent side by side with manual uploads for a sprint.
